title: semantic-prompt-silo-analysis-and-hotfix-log
content:
Context:
This note captures a focused deep dive on three recurrent failure clusters surfaced during the latest onboarding evals for model: open-lite-xxl-v2 (candidate). These failures differ from prior clustering work — they are not simple hallucination spikes or generic calibration shifts. Instead we see semantic "siloing" and cross-prompt interference where different prompt archetypes cause the model to latch on to distinct latent behaviors that conflict when prompts are used together in the same promptset or product flow.

Summary of observed clusters (high-level):
1) semantic-silo-collapse (SSC): model produces internally consistent outputs within one prompt archetype but those outputs are semantically incompatible with other archetypes in the same eval. Example: a "policy-extractor" prompt returns a strict-prescriptive list, while a downstream "tone-normalizer" prompt rewrites it into an overly permissive policy. In isolation each looks fine; together they produce regressions in routing and scoring.
2) style-overlap-interference (SOI): prompts that request stylistic transformations (summarize-as-bullets, formalize, make-concise) intermittently mutate factual delimiters (dates, numeric ranges) leading to subtle but high-impact errors. The error rate is concentrated on prompts containing multi-span lists.
3) role-inversion-edgecase (RIE): model flips speaker intent when the prompt instructs role-play plus instruction chaining ("You are an expert X, then act as Y"). The output preserves role behavior but steps outside the requested guardrails (e.g., providing step-by-step diagnostic actions when asked for high-level guidance).

Quantitative snapshot (from onboarding eval run 2026-01-14):
- dataset size: 3.4k prompt instances across 12 archetypes
- SSC: ~6.8% of prompts flagged (n=232), precision of automated classifier 0.82 (sampled labels)
- SOI: ~9.1% flagged (n=309), concentrated in two archetypes (formalize, summarize-as-bullets)
- RIE: ~3.4% flagged (n=115) but high business weight (avg severity score 4.2/5)
- Aggregate candidate regression lift vs baseline: +2.7% failure rate on onboarding pass metric (primarily SOI + SSC)

Representative examples (anonymized):
- Prompt A (policy-extractor): "List the constraints for return policy in bullet form" -> Model returns: "No returns after 30 days; no refunds for sale items; contact support for exceptions."
- Prompt B (tone-normalizer applied to same text): "Rephrase to be customer-friendly" -> Model outputs: "We accept returns within 30 days and try to help with refunds for sale items; reach out to support." (Introduces permissive language conflicting with the explicit constraint in A)

Hypothesis and root causes:
- Latent mode entanglement: the model appears to learn archetype-specific latent subspaces; when prompts are combined or re-used across a workflow the decoder drifts between subspaces and fails to anchor hard constraints (SSC).
- Training/Alignment gap for list semantics: list formatting and numeric invariants (dates/ranges) are not being prioritized during RLHF/Instruction tuning; this surfaces as SOI where style transforms damage invariants.
- Prompt parsing ambiguity: role prompts often embed nested instructions; the model prefers the most recent persona cue and sometimes promotes low-level actionability even when asked for high-level only (RIE).

Immediate (hotfix) mitigations (low effort, rollback-friendly):
- Per-archetype output constraints: add a light-weight post-filter that checks extracted constraints vs normalized forms and rejects tone-modified outputs that change numeric/date invariants. Implement as a deterministic sanitizer in the serving layer for high-risk archetypes. Owner: Diego. ETA: 1 week.
- Promptset isolation during eval: run archetypes in separate inference pools for canary comparison to measure cross-archetype contamination. This is purely evaluation-time and helps quantify interference. Owner: Zara. ETA: 4 days.
- Conservative decoding for role-chaining prompts: reduce sampling temperature and increase repeat penalty for RIE-prone prompts to force anchor to instruction tokens. Owner: Ethan. ETA: 3 days.

Medium-term experiments (2–8 weeks):
- Instruction anchoring tokens: explore inserting synthetic anchor tokens (e.g., <CONSTRAINTS_BEGIN> ... <CONSTRAINTS_END>) and training a small supervision signal that forces the model to honor bracketed content. Experiment plan: 3-turn fine-tune on curated anchor dataset, A/B vs candidate baseline. Success metric: reduction in SSC breaches by 60% on validation slice. Owner: Priya + Applied ML.
- List-fidelity loss term: augment supervised fine-tuning with an auxiliary loss that penalizes changes to numeric spans and ordered lists. Implementation: synthetic perturbation of lists and label-preservation objective. ETA: 6 weeks. Owner: Research infra.
- Archetype-conditioned prompts: add a meta-token describing archetype and feed it into model context so the model conditions on archetype explicitly rather than inferring from surface cues. Measure whether SOI frequency drops when archetype token is present.

Monitoring and rollback criteria:
- Immediate hotfix post-filter: revert if FPR > 8% on production telemetry or if mean latency increases > 10ms for hot routes.
- Decoding temperature change: roll back if diversity metrics (novel n-gram rate) drop below 40% of baseline or user satisfaction signals decline.
- Fine-tunes: require no increase in overall hallucination rate (>+1.0% absolute) on held-out long-form slice and SSC reduction >= 40% before promoting.

Open questions for triage meeting:
- Are there annotated prompt-level invariants we can productize (numeric/date/list) to speed deterministic checks across product flows?
- How much of SSC is due to dataset mixing in instruction-tuning corpora vs recent RLHF updates? Can we reproduce the effect by mixing two small synthetic archetype datasets?
- Which customer-facing flows are most at risk from RIE outputs (security, billing, compliance); prioritize instrumenting those.

Action items (short):
- Diego: push deterministic invariant sanitizer to eval infra (1 week).
- Zara: run isolated archetype pool evaluation and produce delta report (4 days).
- Ethan: deploy conservative decoding profile for role-chain archetypes to canary (3 days).
- Priya: kick off anchor-token fine-tune experiment and draft evaluation plan (end of week).

Appendix (notes from manual labels):
- Labeling heuristics used for cluster assignment: semantic overlap score (cosine on vectorized outputs), numeric-invariant-change detector (regex + fuzzy match), role-shift score (dialog act classifier).
- Sampling: sampled 120 SSC candidates for hand review — precision ~0.82; action thresholds tuned to prioritize recall for high-severity RIE examples.

This doc is a working log — comments welcome. Next checkpoint: triage + experiment kickoff meeting 2026-02-03.
